newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity settles lower with cash, natgas.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity settles lower with cash, natgas.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled lower Thursday in tandem with plunging spot cash prices and natural gas futures, extending Wednesday's loss tied to milder weather moving into the western U.S.
"People were caught a little bit long on gas," said an East Coast broker.
NYMEX February Henry Hub natgas futures finished down 27.0 cents at $3.341 per million British thermal units.
February gas deliveries to the San Juan/Blanco Hub were notionally assessed at $3.00-$3.04, down from Wednesday's $3.27-$3.31.
In today's cash market, day-ahead power prices at Palo Verde (PV) and California-Oregon Border (COB) fell more than $10.00 a megawatt hour (MWh).
February COB futures finished down 56 cents at $14.65, near the day's low of $14.60. March COB ended dwon 25 cents at $12.35 after bouncing in a 15 cent range.
August and September COB were the most actively traded power contracts today with 168 lots each transacted.
February PV futures finished down 36 cents at $16.99 after traded between $16.85 and $17.15. March PV was inactive at $14.40.

With market fundamentals--mild temperatures and abundant hydroelectric supplies--remaining bearish in the near term, market players expect the complex to continue testing lower end of its recent trading range.
Market sources pegged technical resistance of February COB at $15.00-$15.50 and February PV $18.00.
NYMEX estimated 514 COB and 154 PV contracts were sold.
